'''Vladimir Anastasovich Balabanov''' ({{langx|ru|Влади́мир Анаста́сович Балаба́нов}}, 2 December 1932, Avranlo, [[Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic|Georgian SSR]] — 28 August 2021, [[Thessaloniki]], [[Greece]]) was a [[Soviet]] and [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] mathematician of Greek origin, a [[Doctor of Science|Doctor of Physics and Mathematics]] and a [[professor]].

== Biography ==
Vladimir Balabanov was born on 2 December 1932 in the Greek village called Avranlo in the Georgian SSR.

His father, Anastas Isidorovich Balabanov, worked in Soviet government organizations, while his mother, Sofia Stefanovna Karibova, originates from a family of educators.

In 1950, he graduated from the [[Bolnisi]] Secondary School with a gold medal. In 1954, he graduated with honors from the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics at the Tbilisi Pedagogical Sulkhan-Saba Orbeliani University.

In 1960, he defended his candidate thesis on the topic ''Some Issues of Stability of Solutions of Nonlinear Functional Equations.''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nplg.gov.ge/ec/en/dis/search.html?cmd=search&pft=biblio&qs=700:%D0%91%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B1%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2+%D0%92.%D0%90.|title=NPLG Online Catalogs : Search Result|website=www.nplg.gov.ge|access-date=2021-09-20|archive-date=2021-09-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920212419/http://www.nplg.gov.ge/ec/en/dis/search.html?cmd=search&pft=biblio&qs=700:%D0%91%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B1%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2+%D0%92.%D0%90.}}</ref>

In 1990, he defended his doctoral thesis on the topic ''Some Issues of Nonlinear Functional Analysis and Their Applications.''<ref>{{Cite thesis|url=https://search.rsl.ru/ru/record/01008142060|title=Balabanov, Vladimir Anastasovich - Some Issues of Nonlinear Functional Analysis: Doctoral Dissertation in Physical and Mathematical Sciences: 01.01.01 - Search RSL|website=search.rsl.ru|date=1988 |access-date=2021-09-20|archive-date=2021-09-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920212855/https://search.rsl.ru/ru/record/01008142060}}</ref>

In 1991, he was conferred the academic degree of Doctor of Physical and Mathematical Sciences and the title of professor.<ref>{{Cite web|language=en|url=https://papounidis.com/balabanov-vladimir-anastasovich/|title=Vladimir Anastasovich Balabanov — Doctor of Physical and Mathematical Sciences, Professor|website=Papounidis|date=12 June 2017 |access-date=2021-09-20|archive-date=2021-09-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210920213050/https://papounidis.com/balabanov-vladimir-anastasovich/}}</ref>

Balabanov taught mathematics at several higher-education institutions. He lectured at the Faculty of Physics of [[Tbilisi State University]], the Tbilisi branch of the [[Russian University]] of Cooperation, the [[Tbilisi Institute]] for Teacher Enhancement, the Tbilisi Institute of Economics and Pedagogy, the [[Aristotle University of Thessaloniki]], and the Tbilisi University of Economic Relations.

While living and working in Georgia, Vladimir Balabanov was a member of the Qualification Board of Professors for the Award of Academic Titles and a member of the Board of the Union of Mathematicians of Georgia. By the decree of the President of Georgia [[Eduard Shevardnadze]], he was awarded the ''Order of Honor''.<ref>{{Cite web|language=ka|url=https://matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/110806|title=Tbilisi State University of Ivane Javakhishvili. Professors and Lecturers Honorary Badges and Medals|website=Sakartvelos Sakanonmdeblo Matsne|access-date=2021-09-21|archive-date=2021-09-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921130649/https://matsne.gov.ge/ka/document/view/110806}}</ref> He was also elected an academician of the Greek-Georgian International Humanitarian Academy.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|author=Feodosiy Angelopoulos, Georgiy Yanakidis, Valentin Sardaridis|title=He remained true to his passion|language=English|journal=Mirror Informational and Educational Magazine|type=Magazine|date=November 2007|pages=28–29}}</ref>

Since 2007, he lived with his family in [[Thessaloniki]], [[Greece]].

He was married and had two children.

== Scientific work ==
His primary works were in the field of nonlinear [[functional analysis]] and its applications in [[calculus of variations]], the theory of differential equations, and approximation theory. Some of his research focused on the stability of solutions and bifurcations of solutions of nonlinear operator equations.

He authored more than 70 scientific papers and monographs.

=== Key scientific publications ===
* ''Vladimir Balabanov.'' Some Issues of Nonlinear Functional Analysis and Their Applications. Tbilisi: Metznpereba Publishing, 1982.
* ''Vladimir Balabanov.'' On the Conditional Minimum of a Functional in Topological Vector Spaces // Proceedings of the Tbilisi Mathematical Institute. 1969. No. 36. pp.&nbsp;5–28.
* ''Vladimir Balabanov.'' On Differential Equations in Locally Convex Spaces // Proceedings of Pedagogical Institutes. Georgian SSR Series: Physics and Mathematics. 1978. No. 4. pp.&nbsp;36–45.
* ''Vladimir Balabanov.'' On the Dependence of Solutions of Differential Equations on Perturbations of Initial Conditions and the Right-Hand Side // Proceedings of Pedagogical Institutes. Georgian SSR Series: Physics and Mathematics. 1980. No. 8;
* ''Vladimir Balabanov.'' Filter Structures and Differentiation Operations // Proceedings of the Tbilisi State Pedagogical University named after S. S. Orbeliani. 1997. No. 1. pp.&nbsp;198–207.
* ''Vladimir Balabanov.'' On Topologies Generated by Filter Systems // Proceedings of the Tbilisi State Pedagogical University named after S. S. Orbeliani. 1999. 5. pp.&nbsp;225–230.
* ''Vladimir Balabanov.'' Differentiation of Mappings in Infinite-Dimensional Vector Spaces // Moscow: URSS: KomKniga, 2006. - ISBN 5-484-00384-9<ref>{{Cite book

Scientific achievements were highly appreciated by prominent Soviet scientists of the 20th century, such as Anatoly Skorokhod, Vladilen Trenogin, and Boris Pshenichny.<ref name=":0" />
